subsystems.name: Embodiment interface
subsystems.role: exposes each robot's joints, grippers and sensors through one uniform command and feedback schema, so the same policy can drive different hardware.

subsystems.name: Perception stack
subsystems.role: turns raw sensor data into a representation of objects, poses and contact the policy can act on.

subsystems.name: Behavior model
subsystems.role: maps a plain-language goal plus current observations directly to low-level motor commands.

subsystems.name: Data engine
subsystems.role: supplies the demonstrations and labels that train and keep improving the policy.

subsystems.name: Agent and task layer
subsystems.role: decomposes a goal into steps, calls skills, and recovers when a step fails.

subsystems.name: Safety and fleet layer
subsystems.role: keeps learned control inside hard limits and coordinates many robots in one space.

buildSteps.title: Instrument the robot
buildSteps.detail: Every joint, gripper and camera is wrapped in a driver that conforms to the shared schema and logs observations and commands at control rate.

buildSteps.title: Collect demonstrations
buildSteps.detail: Humans teleoperate the target tasks repeatedly, recording matched observation-action pairs; this is slow, so thousands of episodes are gathered per skill.

buildSteps.title: Normalise across embodiments
buildSteps.detail: Different arm lengths, joint counts and grippers are mapped into a common action space, so one model can learn from data generated on many different robots.

buildSteps.title: Pretrain a vision-language-action model
buildSteps.detail: Training starts from a large pretrained vision-language model, adds an action head, and mixes robot episodes with web-scale image-text data so the model inherits general scene understanding.

buildSteps.title: Fine-tune on the deployment robot
buildSteps.detail: A smaller dataset from the actual machine adapts the policy to its kinematics, camera placement and gripper.

buildSteps.title: Stress test in simulation
buildSteps.detail: Millions of randomised episodes in a physics simulator expose failure modes — slipping, occlusion, unexpected objects — before any hardware is put at risk.

buildSteps.title: Deploy inside a safety envelope
buildSteps.detail: The learned policy runs at a modest rate while a fast classical controller underneath enforces joint limits, force caps and emergency stops.

buildSteps.title: Improve from fleet data
buildSteps.detail: Failures logged in the field are labelled, retrained into the policy, and shipped as updates — the loop that makes the operator more general over time.

prerequisites.why: research systems now translate instructions into robot actions, but generalisation beyond trained tasks and scenes is still weak.
standards such as ROS 2 provide drivers and messaging, though no single API yet covers every commercial arm or mobile base.
cross-institution efforts have pooled over a million robot episodes across more than twenty robot types, but robot data remains tiny next to text and image corpora.
current accelerators are quick enough to run a large policy at the tens-of-hertz rates closed-loop control needs.
rigid-body and some soft-contact dynamics are usable for training, but grasping and deformable objects still transfer poorly to reality.
regulators have no accepted method for certifying a neural network that shares control of a moving machine.

pathway.milestone: single-arm lab policies that follow spoken instructions for a fixed set of tabletop tasks
pathway.unlocks: proof that one model can span several skills instead of one program per task.

pathway.milestone: cross-embodiment models that transfer a learned skill to a robot they were not trained on
pathway.unlocks: an operator that can be pointed at a new machine without bespoke integration.

pathway.milestone: commercial pilots in warehouses and factories with a certified safety supervisor
pathway.unlocks: real deployment data at a scale no lab can generate.

pathway.milestone: a common API and safety case that let one agent run mixed fleets from different vendors
pathway.unlocks: retrofitting existing robots with new competence through software alone.

pathway.milestone: open-ended learning in unstructured settings such as homes and construction
pathway.unlocks: general-purpose physical labour, the point at which the field stops being a demo.
